as_told.title: James Bruce seeks the Ark and brings back the Book of Enoch

plain: The story goes that the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text left out of most Bibles, reached Europe because an explorer named James Bruce brought it back from Ethiopia. The writer Graham Hancock tells it from his own research, pointing to the English translation by R. H. Charles and to Bruce's own account, Travels to Discover the Source of the Nile. Hancock's point is simple: "let's not forget that James Bruce brought something back from Ethiopia he brought back the Book of Enoch." Michels tells it too, in an episode with a guest named Luke Caverns. In his version, Sir James Bruce was a Scottish Freemason, a member of a secretive brotherhood, who went to Ethiopia looking for the Ark of the Covenant, the chest the Bible says held the Ten Commandments, and came home with the Book of Enoch instead. Both tellers raise it because the book describes heavenly beings coming down to Earth, and it reached us by an odd and lucky route.
